implementation: Map<K,H> now owns actual MapNode<K> chains through private OwnedBucketChains<MapNode<K>>, with H retained separately. It no longer delegates to DataMap<K,()> or uses a unit-valued DataMapNode layout.

DataMapStorage<K,V> specializes the same owner to actual DataMapNode<K,V>. The sole canonical BaseMapStorage and real native nodes remain authoritative; no duplicated size/modulus/allocator or ownership registry was introduced.

Shared allocation acquires exact typed node storage before constructor factories, publishes only completed nodes, then increments base count. DataMap construction retains value-before-key order through crate-private construct_parts; Map construction copies only its inherited key.

Shared hash lookup preserves empty skip-hash and growth-before-insertion behavior. Rehash computes native-order destinations before rewiring only real MapLinkNode prefixes, preserving existing item pointer provenance. Its temporary vector is staging, not a second authoritative graph.

Shared removal decrements/unlinks before dropping the exact typed node. Shared Clear drains in native bucket order, reuses deferred panic capture and exact-layout release guard, and replaces allocators only after destroying old nodes.

Sealed unsafe CanonicalMapNode implementations are limited to actual DataMapNode and MapNode layouts. Their Key/Value types account for every owned payload and thread requirement. Private owner Send/Sync is narrowly conditional on those payloads; public erased nodes/base storage gain no blanket impl.

PhantomData<Box<N>> preserves ownership/drop checking, payload covariance and heap-value Unpin. Owner UnwindSafe and RefUnwindSafe retain payload RefUnwindSafe requirements; H retains its independent bound. Thread, negative trait, pinned payload and lifetime covariance tests pass.

Readonly BucketNodeRange and BucketChainPosition are shared between Map/DataMap safe cursors/ranges. Mutable DataMap iteration remains specialized because MapNode Key and Value alias the same object. Its exclusive phantom, advance-before-lend rule and cursor postfix borrow remain intact.

Map Buckets and BasicMapIteratorSource expose actual MapNode<K> pointers; generic KEY_ONLY iteration reads native inherited values, including readonly keys when constructed from a mutable Map. Tests inspect the actual facade nodes and compare native dereference/Key/arrow identity.

Map duplicate Add uses a shared node projection, avoiding an unnecessary mutable whole-node retag. End constructs the native empty cursor directly without traversing keys. Native copy/Assign and Rust clone_from keep their distinct allocator/hasher/table behavior.

Restored cursor doctests and existing comments were preserved; all259TKerneldoctests passed. Shared collision-hash fixture was extracted for Map/DataMap matrices, and dead private DataMap key-only facade code was removed.

DataMapNode::key_mut remains available for the coordinated IndexedDataMapNode::Key1 consumer. The temporary narrow dead_code allowance documents that concurrent dependency; construct_parts has the identical crate-private visibility change required by that branch.
safety_extensions: Rust hash panics leave old canonical chains intact before publishing a rehash. Rust destructor panics finish remaining node cleanup and allocator release before resuming the first panic. These guarantees are outside ordinary native noexcept destruction behavior.
Over-aligned and zero-sized Rust keys/values are supported without claiming ABI equivalence for every C++ empty class or custom type. Native fixture exercises ordinary integer keys.

Finite constructor/copy fixtures do not close every C++ custom move-assignment hook or variadic template argument pack. Native API declaration candidates remain pending exact compiler/Rustdoc resolution.
remaining_gaps: Measured existing DataMap tail-padding gap: native int/int,char/int,int/char nodes have size16 align8 Key offset12 Value8, but Rust nested ListValueNode fields give size24 Key16. Native char/char has size16 Key9 Value8 versus Rust size24 Key16. Therefore native DataMap allocation-byte and complete subobject layout parity is NOT achieved by this migration. A separate flattening correction is required.

MapNode<int>,MapNode<char>,MapNode<double> match native/Rust size16 align8 Key8 and ListValueNode size16 on this pinned Linux compiler build. Four tested DataMap larger-key/value layouts also match, but this finite comparison proves no universal C++ ABI claim.

Existing DataMapNode source wording about preserving layout must be narrowed during the separately assigned layout correction: the current prefix at offset0 is real, but nested full-base padding prevents native derived-key tail reuse. Production sources were intentionally left frozen after the measured discovery.

Sound reentrant callback observer provenance remains unimplemented. The prior native count/allocator observer rows remain unjoined; correct operation ordering and post-operation state alone do not close that observer contract.

Arbitrary user-derived protected base operations and every template instantiation remain outside this concrete facade/engine proof. Normal unordered Map/DataMap generic iterator specializations are tested; ordered template variants for these unordered containers are not claimed.
Other hash-map families still need their own canonical node/base storage migrations. No global API inventory or legacy declaration credit is assigned by this scoped receipt.
